posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
But, but wait.....I thought that no idea can be criticised. I'm frequently told, right on these pages, that "ideas" should be unconditionally accepted, indeed encouraged, because they serve to promote and inspire people into new ways of thinking. I'm also frequently told that nothing is impossible and I have been criticised when I label "ideas" as bunk. 

Yes, this stuff has been around since the 60's (where's my flying car?? .) Yes it's complete bunk and total rhetoric. Yes, he's going to get millions of dollars to develop this bunk. Yes, small-time, genuine holographers are the real "people scraping crumbs from the floor". If we, as holographers, or anyone else, don't caste a jaundiced and critical eye at "ideas" we stand to promote yet more, and yet more bizarre, "ideas" to the detriment of real holography, or any other technology. Maybe the one good to come out of it is that "holography" seems to be getting more and more in the public consciousness. Now if we could only capitulate on this, instead of allowing pseudo- and wannabe scientists to hijack the word "holography".

By the way, he didn't mention "Einstein" or "Unified Field Theory", or even "Cold Fusion". He did mention "Electromagnetic Radiation". Oh, and you don't need to stare at the Aurora Borealis to "see" "Electromagnetic Radiation". Take a burnt match, wrap a piece of tinfoil tightly around it and put it in your microwave. Do not try this at home.
